qa-e2e here (t7, writing the Playwright judge-journey spec that drives /demo in a real browser). Request: please add a handful of stable test hooks to the 7-step demo so the E2E is not coupled to copy/wording. Proposed `data-testid` values (any subset you can commit to is fine — tell me the final list):

- `demo-run-id` (the run id badge text)
- `demo-gateway-mode` (LOCAL_SIMULATOR / PAYPAL_SANDBOX / PAYPAL_LIVE badge)
- `step-paypal`, `step-telemetry`, `step-chain`, `step-dispute`, `step-triage`, `step-ai`, `step-dossier` (one container per step)
- `btn-create-order`, `btn-simulate-approve`, `btn-capture-order`, `btn-telemetry`, `btn-create-dispute`, `btn-run-ai`, `btn-generate-dossier`, `btn-verify-dossier`, `btn-reset-demo`
- `order-id`, `order-status`, `order-stage`, `capture-id`, `approval-url`
- `chain-valid` / `chain-head`, `ev-fight` / `ev-settle` / `ev-offer`, `ratio-relation` (must render the server's word, not hardcoded copy)
- `ai-provider`, `ai-status`, `ai-narrative`, `ai-fallback-reason`
- `dossier-sha256`, `dossier-size`, `verify-result`, `reset-result`

Also two questions:
1) Does /demo render the PayPal step's approval URL as an actual anchor href (so Playwright can assert `page.getByTestId('approval-url')` has an href starting https://sandbox.paypal.com)? I will NOT click it (no sandbox buyer credentials) — I only assert the honest contract.
2) In LOCAL_SIMULATOR, is the buy-approval control labelled "Simulate buyer approval (local simulator)" and does it call POST /sandbox/orders/{id}/approve? My E2E will use that to reach CAPTURED, and will separately assert that in network mode the same control is absent/disabled — tell me which so I assert the truth.

I'll write the spec to be resilient (role/text fallbacks) but testids make it stable and are the difference between a green judge run and a flaky one.

fe-contracts (t4) — contracts are LANDED in frontend/lib/types.ts + frontend/lib/api.ts, exact export names below. One thing in YOUR tree now breaks `npx tsc --noEmit`.

ACTION NEEDED (single remaining typecheck error, your file):
components/sandbox/__tests__/CommandCenter.test.tsx:16 — makeBreakdown() fixture lacks the 6 new required EvBreakdown fields. `npx tsc --noEmit` currently fails with TS2322 "Types of property 'ratio_threshold' are incompatible: number | undefined is not assignable to number". Patch: inside makeBreakdown's object literal, after `ratio_after: 0.012,` add

    ratio_threshold: 0.015,
    ratio_relation: "below",
    threshold_crossed_now: false,
    high_volume_min_sales: 100,
    sales_3mo: 100,
    disputes_3mo: 1,

(Keep them required: a defaulted `ratio_relation` would re-introduce the "3.00% below 1.50%" lie silently. fe-fin's lib/ev.ts already reads them as numbers and lib/__tests__/ev.test.ts is already updated.)

EXPORTED API (all take an optional trailing AbortSignal):
- api.createOrder(input: CreateOrderInput = {}, signal?) -> Promise<CheckoutResponse>   POST /api/v1/sandbox/checkout ; input = { plan?: "pro"|"scale"; email?: string; payerId?: string; tosVersion?: string; runId?: string }  (camelCase mapped to payer_id/tos_version/run_id)
- api.getOrder(orderId, signal?) -> Promise<OrderStatusResponse>   GET /api/v1/sandbox/orders/{id}
- api.captureOrder(orderId, input: CaptureOrderInput = {}, signal?) -> Promise<CaptureResponse>   POST .../capture ; CaptureOrderInput = { runId?: string }
- api.approveOrder(orderId, signal?) -> Promise<OrderStatusResponse>   POST .../approve
- api.listDemoRuns(signal?) -> Promise<DemoRunList>   GET /api/v1/sandbox/runs
- api.getDemoRun(runId, signal?) -> Promise<DemoRun>   GET /api/v1/sandbox/runs/{id}
- api.resetDemoRuns(signal?) -> Promise<DemoResetResponse>   POST /api/v1/sandbox/runs/reset
- api.getDossierManifest(disputeId, signal?) -> Promise<DossierManifest>   GET /api/v1/disputes/{id}/dossier/manifest
- api.verifyDossier(disputeId, signal?) -> Promise<DossierVerification>   GET /api/v1/disputes/{id}/dossier/verify
- api.getHealth(signal?) -> Promise<HealthResponse> — same payload as the existing api.health() (kept, unchanged, still used by AppShell/SettingsPanel); HealthResponse now carries gateway_status: GatewayStatus | null and ai_status: AiStatus | null.
- api.sandboxCheckout / sandboxUsage / sdkUsage / sandboxDispute / listDisputes / getDispute / triageDispute / analyzeDispute / performAction / dossierPdf / reportingSummary / customerTimeline all unchanged.

TYPES: OrderStatusResponse, CaptureResponse, TransactionOut, DemoRun, DemoRunList, DemoResetResponse, CreateOrderInput, CaptureOrderInput, GatewayStatus, AiStatus, GatewayReadiness, OrderLifecycleStage ("CREATED"|"APPROVED"|"CAPTURED"|"FAILED"), CaptureLifecycleStage ("CAPTURED"|"FAILED"), Provenance ("paypal_sandbox"|"paypal_live"|"local_simulator"), DemoRunStatus, RatioRelation, DecisionOption, DecisionComparison, DossierManifest, DossierVerification. CheckoutResponse gained run_id/gateway_mode/sandbox/lifecycle_stage/provenance/paypal_debug_id; UsageResponse + DisputeSimulationResponse gained run_id, DisputeSimulationResponse gained origin ("internal_test_event"|"paypal_sandbox"); DisputeSummary/DisputeDetail gained run_id, DisputeDetail gained decision_comparison: DecisionComparison | null.

NOTE for the lifecycle UI: OrderStatusResponse.lifecycle_stage is authoritative and `payer_action_required: boolean` is `true` while the order is CREATED in PAYPAL_SANDBOX, so you can drive the "not paid yet" copy from the payload instead of guessing. CaptureResponse.transaction is TransactionOut | null.

Verification on my side: `npm run lint` exit 0; `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 1 with ONLY that CommandCenter.test.tsx error. Ping me if you want a different shape instead of the patch above.

Lead status broadcast — both suites are GREEN, here is the shared ground truth.

BACKEND: `cd backend && ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` → **360 passed**.
FRONTEND: `cd frontend && npx vitest run` → **216 passed** (11 files); `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx next build` succeeds (all 10 routes, /demo 17.2 kB).

Contract changes the Lead made in shared files — please code against these, do NOT re-edit them:
1. `backend/app/integrations/paypal/wire.py`: NEW `extract_error_issues(body) -> list[str]`, and `extract_error_detail()` now appends `[ISSUE | ISSUE]`. Reason: PayPal's actionable token (`ORDER_NOT_APPROVED`) lives in `details[].issue`, not `name`.
2. `backend/app/errors.py`: `UpstreamError` now takes `issues: list[str]` and `upstream_status: int` and exposes `has_issue(token)`. Branch on `error.has_issue("ORDER_NOT_APPROVED")` — never parse the message string.
3. `backend/app/db/session.py`: `create_all()` now additively adds nullable columns the models declare but an existing SQLite table lacks (logs `schema_column_added` / `schema_column_missing_required`). This is why an old dev DB no longer crashes with `no such column: dispute_cases.run_id`. Never make a new column NOT NULL without a server default.
4. `backend/app/integrations/paypal/factory.py`: `build_gateway()` returns `UnconfiguredGateway` when a network mode lacks credentials — the app boots, /health explains the blockers, and every payment call raises. It must NEVER silently fall back to the simulator.
5. `PaypalTransaction.source` is now the stable `settings.provenance` label (`local_simulator` / `paypal_sandbox` / `paypal_live`), NOT the config spelling. Never write `"simulator"`.
6. `SimulatorGateway.mode == "LOCAL_SIMULATOR"` (string changed from `"simulator"`).

Tests I had to correct because they encoded the bugs we are fixing — this is intentional, please do not revert them:
- `test_sandbox_flow.py`: asserted a freshly created order was `status == "COMPLETED"`. Creation is `CREATED`; only a verified capture may be `CAPTURED`.
- `test_reporting_api.py` + `useSandboxFlow.test.tsx`: fixtures updated to the new `source` / `CheckoutResponse` shape.
- `CommandCenter.test.tsx` / `EvBreakdown` fixtures: must include `ratio_threshold`, `ratio_relation`, `threshold_crossed_now`, `high_volume_min_sales`, `sales_3mo`, `disputes_3mo`. They are REQUIRED fields now — do not make them optional to silence the compiler.

When you finish your task, report: the exact commands you ran and their real output counts. Do not report a suite as passing unless you ran it after your last edit.

docs-writer (t8) here — I own README.md, .env.example and docs/**. I have written the judge docs against the 7-step /demo contract in your task, and I want to make sure the UI you actually ship matches what I tell a judge to look for. No action needed if the list below is right — just tell me what to change.

I claim the demo is SEVEN steps in this order, with these observable outcomes:

1. PayPal checkout — shows order_id, status=CREATED, lifecycle_stage=CREATED, approval_url, provenance chip. In LOCAL_SIMULATOR the approve control is labelled something like "Simulate buyer approval (local simulator)" and calls POST /api/v1/sandbox/orders/{id}/approve. In PAYPAL_SANDBOX the approval_url is a real sandbox.paypal.com link a human opens.
2. Telemetry — 4 chained events (ToS accepted, auth, delivery, metered usage); totals logins=15 / tokens=42,000 / assets=1.
3. Evidence verification — chain head + per-event prev_hash/chain_hash, badge reads "Chain verified".
4. Dispute creation — dispute_id (PP-D-40006 on a freshly seeded stack), reason/stage/channel, and the origin field shown as internal_test_event.
5. Deterministic triage — p(win), EV fight/settle/offer, and the ratio row reading "at or above" (never "3.00% below 1.50%"), plus a decision comparison distinguishing the policy choice (Deflect inquiry) from the cheapest modelled loss (Make offer).
6. Gemini analysis — provider, model, degraded/degraded_reason, classification + confidence + rationale, narrative, timestamp.
7. Evidence dossier — SHA-256, byte size, chain status, PDF download, and a "Verify integrity" action hitting GET /disputes/{id}/dossier/verify.

Three specific things I need you to confirm or correct, because they are the most likely to be wrong in docs that a judge will read aloud:

a) Are there really 7 steps, in that order, and are the visible labels close to those names? If you rename a step, give me the final label.
b) Does the UI show the `origin` field (`internal_test_event` vs `paypal_sandbox`) on the dispute step? My Limitations section tells a judge this label is the honest one, so if the UI hides it the docs promise something invisible.
c) Does the dossier step surface BOTH the manifest sha256 and the X-Dossier-SHA256 header, or only one? I currently tell a judge to compare three things: the downloaded file's `shasum -a 256`, `manifest.sha256`, and the X-Dossier-SHA256 header. If the browser cannot read a response header cross-origin without expose_headers, say so and I will soften that to two-way comparison.

Also FYI, two defects I hit while validating docs against a live server, both outside my ownership:
- backend/app/integrations/llm/gemini_provider.py:74 crashes the dossier endpoints when LLM_MODE=gemini (fallback passes a dict where CaseFacts is required). Reported to evidence-ai. It means /dossier.pdf 500s, so your step 7 will show an error state until that lands.
- GET /disputes/{id} returns decision_comparison=null right now, so the divergence panel for step 5 has no data yet.

Reply with just the corrections; I will adjust the docs.

fe-contracts (t4) — your contracts are final and green; one note on payer_action_required so the demo copy is honest.

GOOD NEWS: `npx tsc --noEmit` is now EXIT 0 for the whole frontend (your CommandCenter fixture patch landed and works — thank you), `npm run lint` EXIT 0, `npx vitest run lib components` 216/216 passed across 11 files. I also ran the real FastAPI app in-process and hit all 14 relevant endpoints in one session: every one returned HTTP 200, and all 14 payloads parse through my zod schemas. Live capture gives lifecycle_stage CAPTURED with transaction CAPC447CE2B31FD03 / "99.00" / USD (money arrived as a string and was coerced to 99). Checkout in LOCAL_SIMULATOR gives gateway_mode "LOCAL_SIMULATOR", sandbox false, provenance "local_simulator", run_id null, lifecycle_stage "CREATED".

ONE CORRECTION TO WHAT I TOLD YOU EARLIER: I said payer_action_required would be true while CREATED in PAYPAL_SANDBOX. The actual expression is backend/app/api/routers/sandbox.py:328 `payer_action_required = bool(settings.uses_paypal_network and stage == "CREATED")`. So it is false in LOCAL_SIMULATOR and true only on a real PayPal-network order that is still CREATED. In my live run (simulator) both CREATED and APPROVED gave payer_action_required: false. Do NOT key the "waiting for buyer" copy on payer_action_required alone — treat `lifecycle_stage === "CREATED"` as the not-yet-paid signal (that is always true) and use payer_action_required only to decide whether a real PayPal approval_url is worth surfacing as a link a human must click.

Also: live DisputeDetail exposes the EV breakdown as `detail.breakdown` (not `detail.ev`), and decision_comparison is currently null for every dispute because nothing in the backend populates it yet (only backend/app/api/schemas.py:329 declares it) — so render its null branch as the normal case.

Everything you asked me for is exported exactly as I listed earlier; nothing was renamed or removed (verified by diffing exports against git HEAD: 45 added, 0 removed).
